title: Public-Facing Application Exploits
overview: Inspect a web application firewall finding against the telemetry of a fictional public application.
prerequisites: Be comfortable reading timestamps and network sensor or waf projection fields.

attack.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: A blocked request classified as injection on an exposed route merits a review for origin-side impact.
evidence: Check WAF action, signature family, route and origin status. Look for paired application errors in an owned environment.
false_positive: A penetration test or scanner authorized for that service can trip the same rule.
tuning: Restrict approved-test exceptions by source and time. Retain blocked events for trend analysis.
response: Preserve WAF and origin logs, correlate request IDs, and verify the affected application version and patch status.
prevention: Reduce exposure, maintain a patch SLA and monitor WAF policy changes.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The fixture contains a classification only. It contains no request payload or evidence of successful exploitation.

questions.prompt: What does the WAF verdict show?
questions.explanation: Blocked activity supports triage, while origin evidence establishes impact.
Origin logs can show whether the request reached and affected the service.
